chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad Al-Nawfaly, from the offspring of Nawfal ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who said: He informed me, Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Isa from Abdullah al-Umari from his father from his grandfather who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding the illness that befalls the child, he said: It is an expiation for his parents.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of a child's illness in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates that illnesses afflicting a child serve as an expiation (*kaffarah*) for their parents' sins, reflecting the Shia understanding of divine mercy and the interconnectedness of familial spiritual states. This concept is often contextualized within the broader theological discussion of *saghir* (minor sins) being purified through worldly trials, distinguishing it from the expiation of major sins which may require specific acts of worship or divine forgiveness. The chain of transmission highlights the scholarly lineage connecting the Prophet's household to the early Imams, reinforcing the authority of this practical guidance in daily religious life.
